tool_result.text:
---
policy_id: POL-AP-004
title: Quantity Variance and Delivery Discrepancies
owner: Group Financial Controller
effective_from: 2025-04-01
applies_to: Supplier invoices matched to a purchase order and goods receipt
---

# Quantity Variance and Delivery Discrepancies

## Three-way match

Invoices raised against a purchase order are matched on three documents: the purchase
order, the goods receipt note, and the invoice. Quantity is assessed **against the goods
receipt**, not against the purchase order.

## Under-delivery

Where the invoiced quantity is lower than the quantity ordered, and the goods receipt
confirms that the lower quantity was received, the invoice is correct as presented and
represents either:

- a **short delivery**, where the balance is not expected; or
- a **partial invoice**, where the balance remains outstanding on the purchase order and
  will be invoiced separately.

The two are distinguished by whether the purchase order remains open for the balance and
whether the supplier has previously invoiced partially against the same order. Accounts
Payable should establish which applies before processing, as the treatment of the
purchase order differs.

## Over-delivery

Where the invoiced quantity exceeds the quantity ordered:

- if the goods receipt confirms the higher quantity was received and accepted, an
  over-delivery tolerance of ten per cent (10%) of the ordered quantity may be accepted;
- beyond that, the invoice is referred to the raising cost centre.

## Units of measure

Quantity and price must be assessed on a consistent unit of measure. Where the purchase
order and the invoice express quantity in different units, the invoice is not to be
treated as a variance until the units have been reconciled.

tool_result.text:
---
policy_id: POL-AP-001
title: Invoice Price Tolerance
owner: Group Financial Controller
effective_from: 2025-04-01
applies_to: All supplier invoices matched to a purchase order
---

# Invoice Price Tolerance

## Purpose

To permit efficient processing of supplier invoices where the invoiced price differs
immaterially from the price agreed on the purchase order, without requiring manual
intervention for every minor variance.

## Standard tolerance

Where the invoiced unit price exceeds the purchase order unit price, Accounts Payable
may accept the invoice without escalation provided the variance does **not exceed five
per cent (5%)** of the purchase order unit price.

Variances of any size in the supplier's favour to the buyer — that is, an invoiced price
*below* the purchase order price — are accepted without escalation.

## Where the standard tolerance does not apply

The tolerance in this policy is the organisation's default position. It applies **except
where a more specific commercial arrangement is in force with the supplier**, in which
case the terms of that arrangement prevail. See POL-AP-002.

The standard tolerance does not apply to:

- capital equipment purchases, which are governed by the capital approval framework;
- suppliers whose account is on hold;
- suppliers whose commercial agreement has lapsed.

## Cumulative variance

Where a single invoice contains multiple lines, tolerance is assessed **per line**.
An invoice may therefore be partially within tolerance. Where the aggregate variance
across the invoice exceeds five per cent of the invoice total, the invoice should be
escalated in full even where individual lines are within tolerance.
